claim: Azure regions and availability zones are the equivalent of AWS Regions and Availability Zones (AZ-900 crosswalk).
reason: The Microsoft Learn AWS-to-Azure comparison pages do not list regions or availability zones. Source it from Microsoft Learn and AWS global infrastructure docs in Step 2, including where the analogy breaks.
resolution: Azure side confirmed on its dedicated Microsoft Learn page (2026-10-08); the AWS side is cited in the Step 2 notes.

claim: The Azure shared responsibility model corresponds to the AWS shared responsibility model (AZ-900 crosswalk).
reason: Not covered by the Learn comparison pages. Source it from Microsoft Learn and AWS docs in Step 2.
resolution: Azure side confirmed on its dedicated Microsoft Learn page (2026-10-08); the AWS side is cited in the Step 2 notes.

claim: Azure storage redundancy options (LRS, ZRS, GRS) correspond to S3 and EBS durability and replication choices (AZ-900 crosswalk).
reason: The Learn storage comparison page covers services and tiers, not redundancy options. Source it from Microsoft Learn and AWS docs in Step 2.
resolution: Azure side confirmed on its dedicated Microsoft Learn page (2026-10-08); the AWS side is cited in the Step 2 notes.

claim: Amazon Quick (named in the exam guide, task 3.5) is the product the Learn comparison page calls Amazon QuickSight.
reason: The two allowed sources use different names. Confirm the current product name in AWS docs before writing Step 2 notes; keep the guide's wording in questions.

claim: The exam guide labels 2.2-K2 'AWS Managed Services (AMS)' but gives Amazon Comprehend and Amazon Polly as examples.
reason: Comprehend and Polly are pre-built AI services, while AWS Managed Services (AMS) is a separate operations offering that is not on the guide's in-scope list. The notes treat the bullet as 'managed AWS services with appropriate use cases' and teach Comprehend and Polly; no AWS page confirms the intended meaning of 'AMS' here.

claim: AWS Auto Scaling (scaling plans) is current and recommended alongside Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling.
reason: The exam guide lists 'AWS Auto Scaling' but its documentation page now leads to a guide for migrating a scaling plan to EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Auto Scaling scaling policies. No allowed page states whether scaling plans are retired. The notes teach EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Auto Scaling policies and report only what the migration page says.

claim: AWS Snow Family devices are available for new transfer designs.
reason: The exam guide lists AWS Snow Family, but the Snowball Edge documentation states AWS Snowball Edge is no longer available to new customers and points new customers to AWS DataSync, AWS Data Transfer Terminal or partner solutions. No allowed page tells which Snow devices (such as Snowcone) remain available. The notes label Snowball Edge accordingly and teach the transfer-method choice; the exam may still use Snow Family wording.

claim: S3 Standard-IA and S3 One Zone-IA have a 30-day minimum storage duration.
reason: The S3 storage classes page states a 30-day minimum and a 128 KB minimum charge. The AWS storage decision guide, updated 5 October 2026, says S3 no longer applies a 30-day minimum storage duration for transitions to these two classes. The two statements are recorded as c-s3-ia-minimum-duration. Re-check both pages before any question uses the figure.

claim: Whether Amazon Timestream for LiveAnalytics is open to new customers.
reason: The Timestream for LiveAnalytics page says: for similar capabilities, consider Amazon Timestream for InfluxDB. No allowed page checked states clearly whether LiveAnalytics accepts new customers. The notes quote the page's wording and teach the time series data type, and do not claim a retirement. Re-check before any question names Timestream for LiveAnalytics.
resolution: The Timestream for LiveAnalytics availability change page (2026-10-09) states AWS closed new customer access, that existing workloads are not affected, and recommends Timestream for InfluxDB for new customers. The notes quote it (source timestream-availability).

claim: AWS Global Accelerator does not cache content.
reason: No allowed AWS page checked states this directly. The Global Accelerator FAQ contrasts it with CloudFront (CloudFront improves cacheable and dynamic content; Global Accelerator proxies TCP or UDP packets at the edge and suits non-HTTP, static IP and fast regional failover use cases). The Express notes now quote that contrast and no longer say 'does not cache'; wording in other districts or Don't confuse pairs should do the same unless an AWS page states it.

claim: Amazon Data Firehose delivery corresponds to Azure Event Hubs Capture.
reason: The Microsoft Learn analytics comparison has no Firehose row and does not mention Event Hubs Capture, so the notes say only that Learn lists no Firehose counterpart. No allowed page confirms the mapping.

claim: RDS Multi-AZ failover is automatic and keeps the same endpoint, while promoting a read replica is a manual step that gives the replica its own endpoint.
reason: The Multi-AZ and read replica pages checked do not state the endpoint behaviour in a quotable sentence (the replica page says only that you can promote a replica to a standalone instance). Left out of the Express notes until a quotable AWS sentence is found.

claim: AWS Security Hub (named in the exam guide, task 1.2) is the product the current AWS documentation calls AWS Security Hub CSPM.
reason: The Security Hub User Guide page is titled 'Introduction to AWS Security Hub CSPM' and describes AWS Security Hub Cloud Security Posture Management (AWS Security Hub CSPM); no allowed page checked states that this is a rename of the service the exam guide lists as AWS Security Hub, or whether the exam guide name now covers a wider offering. The notes use the page's own name 'AWS Security Hub CSPM' for the checks-and-findings behaviour that its quotes describe and do not claim a rename. Re-check before any question names Security Hub.

claim: Shield Advanced offers DDoS cost protection (credits for scaling charges caused by a DDoS attack).
reason: The Shield Advanced pages read (ddos-advanced-summary and its capabilities page) state that the subscription covers the costs of standard AWS WAF capabilities for protected resources, but the pages checked do not use the words 'cost protection' for usage-spike credits. The notes state only the WAF-cost coverage that the page quotes.

claim: Certificates for edge-optimized API Gateway custom domain names must also be requested or imported in US East (N. Virginia).
reason: The ACM and CloudFront pages state the US East (N. Virginia) rule for CloudFront only. The ACM integrated-services page mentions custom domain names for API Gateway without giving the Region rule. The notes state the rule for CloudFront only.

claim: Direct Connect takes weeks to provision, and MACsec offers Layer 2 encryption on dedicated connections.
reason: Not confirmed on the Direct Connect pages checked for this pass (Welcome and Encryption in AWS Direct Connect). The notes state only that Direct Connect does not encrypt traffic in transit by default and that combining it with Site-to-Site VPN gives an IPsec-encrypted private connection.

claim: Aurora Serverless v1 reached end of life on a specific date (reviewer recalled 31 March 2025) and was replaced by Aurora Serverless v2.
reason: The live Aurora pages checked (2026-10-09) no longer carry the v1 end-of-life notice; the only live statement found is on the Aurora serverless how-it-works page: Aurora Serverless v1 is a deprecated product with a different architecture. The notes quote that wording, label it deprecated and give no date. Current pages name the product just 'Aurora serverless'. Re-check for an AWS page stating the date before any question uses it.

claim: Database Savings Plans offer the same one- and three-year terms and All/Partial/No upfront payment options as Compute and EC2 Instance Savings Plans.
reason: The Savings Plans comparison page states one or three year terms for the Compute and EC2 Instance plans; the plan types page lists Database Savings Plans and what they cover but no allowed page checked states their term or payment options. The notes state the generic one-or-three-year term and payment options only from the Savings Plans overview and do not claim them per plan type. Re-check before any question depends on a Database Savings Plan term.

claim: Activating a cost allocation tag is not retroactive: costs incurred before activation are not attributed to the tag.
reason: The cost allocation tags page says only that activated tags organise costs on the report and that tags can take up to 24 hours to appear; it does not state the retroactivity rule. Not added to the notes. Re-check on the Billing and Cost Management user guide.

claim: Objects must stay a minimum time in S3 Standard before a lifecycle rule can transition them to Standard-IA or One Zone-IA.
reason: The lifecycle transition page checked states the minimum-duration rule only for leaving a class (a single rule cannot move objects out of a class before its minimum storage duration) and the storage decision guide says S3 no longer applies a 30-day minimum for transitions to the two IA classes. The reviewer's claim is not stated on an allowed page and conflicts with the decision guide, so it is not in the notes; see c-s3-ia-minimum-duration.
